questions.a: 'has been teaching' / 'has taught' — 'for' demands the perfect family. A wrong answer 'is teaching' anchors to present and ignores the duration marker entirely.

questions.q: 'I ___ (not understand) this chapter — please explain again.'
questions.a: 'do not understand' — stative verb, no continuous. A wrong answer 'am not understanding' is the stative-ing error that markers cannot excuse.

questions.q: 'The train had left before we reached' — which event is earlier, and which tense marks it?
questions.a: The leaving is earlier, marked by past perfect 'had left'. A wrong answer saying 'reached' is earlier shows the student reads clauses in order rather than using 'before' to order events.

questions.q: CBSE class 9 tests tense through gap-fills and editing, not definitions: the examiners' tools are ______ (since, for, by the time, while, already, yet), stative verbs (know, believe, own — no -ing), and two-event ordering (earlier past = past perfect).

Fill in the blank: CBSE class 9 tests tense through gap-fills and editing, not ______: the examiners' tools are time-markers (since, for, by the time, while, already, yet), stative verbs (know, believe, own — no -ing), and two-event ordering (earlier past = past perfect).

Fill in the blank: The exam pattern: every tense item hides a marker. 'I ___ here since 2019' — 'since' demands perfect. 'While she ___ , the phone rang' — 'while' demands ______ background. 'The train ___ before we reached' — 'before' demands past perfect on the earlier event.

Fill in the blank: The exam pattern: every tense item hides a marker. 'I ___ here since ______' — 'since' demands perfect. 'While she ___ , the phone rang' — 'while' demands continuous background. 'The train ___ before we reached' — 'before' demands past perfect on the earlier event.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student selects correct tense forms in gap-fill items by reading markers first, avoids stative-continuous errors, and orders two past events with past perfect.
